ops.title: P5/P6 re-scoped against cc-orchestrate v0.3.0 (user-ratified)
ops.body:
Recon (cc-orchestrate @7da2dcb) invalidated the original P5/P6 wording: `childMCPConfig` is gone (child `--mcp-config` flags intentionally removed; channel MCP rides an installed plugin via `--channels`), `childSettings` survives but is hooks-only, `channelsetup` is hoisted approval infra (not a plugin-injection API — do not build on it), and the supervisor is already three-signal (membership + backend prober + 45s-grace/2-min transcript-staleness). User picked (2026-07-17, AskUserQuestion):

- **P5 = launcher knob + reuse wrap.** cc-orchestrate gains one generic child-launcher-prefix config knob applied in `claudeInvocation` so it covers `claudeCommand` AND `resumeCommand` symmetrically; set to `cc-runtime wrap --`, the existing E2E-tested wrap does plugin injection + native-tool disable. cc-orchestrate stays tool-agnostic — invariant reworded: no cc-runtime tool names in *code* and no `interaction` import (the pre-existing `AskUserQuestion` literal in status.go:144 transcript classification is out of scope). Must compose with the `ccp run` prefix, pty-host wrap, and scrub-exec.
- **P6 = explicit pty child-exit signal.** `ptyhost.Run` learns a child-exit event the supervisor consumes as an immediate authoritative death signal (today exit surfaces only indirectly via membership); prober + staleness stay as native-backend fallbacks. Detection latency: ~2min → instant.
